extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on verifying online content (images, videos, posts) in real time so consumers and reporters can tell whether material is doctored or genuine. Based on investigative techniques used by a newsroom team to authenticate social media content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sort through the deluge of online content
rubrics_metrics.description: How to manage and triage the huge and growing volume of online material (e.g., millions of photos and hours of video uploaded every hour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The talk frames the problem quantitatively (more hours of video, millions more photos) to motivate techniques for prioritizing what to verify; no specific triage algorithm provided on the page text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify information in real-time
rubrics_metrics.description: Use investigative techniques to verify information as it appears online so audiences can quickly know whether a claim or piece of media is true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes real-time verification methods used by the speaker and his team, intended to provide timely judgment on circulating content; specific techniques are described in the talk (not in the page blurb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect doctored images
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether an image has been manipulated or doctored (example given: 'that Statue of Liberty image has been doctored').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image-authentication is called out as a distinct verification task; the page notes this as an example of what the speaker's techniques can reveal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate video provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether videos circulating online are legitimate and accurately sourced (example given: 'if that video leaked from Syria is legitimate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video-origin checks and provenance assessment are highlighted as a core verification goal; the page indicates the talk covers techniques to make such determinations in real time.
